articles.title: ConocoPhillips to Exit Norway in $4.43 Billion Deal with Vaar Energi
articles.description: Vaar Energi has agreed to buy ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian business in a $4.43 billion deal that includes Ekofisk, the field that launched Norway’s oil era, and stakes in some of the country’s largest gas fields. Vaar Energi said Monday it had agreed to acquire interests in 13 producing fields and related infrastructure in Norway and the United Kingdom. The portfolio includes the Greater Ekofisk Area, stakes in Troll, Heidrun, Oseberg and Aasta Hansteen, and the Teesside oil terminal in northeast England. The sale would end ConocoPhillips’…

articles.title: Why Blocking the Sun Won't Solve the Climate Crisis
articles.description: When people think about geoengineering the climate to stall or reverse climate change, they often think of university and government research labs. Given the scope and importance of such a project, it only seems natural that governments would be the ones to implement such a momentous and fraught project. But there is now a new player on the scene: private companies promoting their technologies and capabilities to block sunlight in order to reduce the temperature of the Earth. I've opined previously about the dangers of altering the amount of sunlight…

articles.title: Pakistan and Iran Move to Boost Energy Cooperation
articles.description: Pakistan and Iran are nearing the creation of a joint working group to boost energy cooperation, with a focus on electricity supply and electricity transmission projects, Pakistani outlet Business Recorder reported on Monday, quoting sources with knowledge of the matter. The two allies are doing preparatory work to set up a joint working group on electricity and energy, expected to feature discussions on financing for the second phase of Pakistan’s Gwadar electricity transmission line that is planned to increase Iranian electricity exports…

articles.title: The Energy Transition Needs More Metals but Less Extraction
articles.description: The energy transition is often described as a switch from one extraction industry to another. Instead of digging up coal and drilling for oil, the argument goes, we will simply dig up enormous quantities of lithium, copper and nickel. There is some truth in that description. More mines will be needed for several important metals. But it misses the much larger change taking place underneath. A renewable and electrified energy system can require substantially less ongoing extraction than the fossil system it replaces. The world can need more copper…

articles.title: Western Australia Offers New Oil, Carbon Storage Exploration Areas
articles.description: Western Australia has opened license applications for seven petroleum exploration areas and four areas for greenhouse gas storage exploration.

articles.title: Japan’s Electricity Prices Surge to 2022 High as Cold Weather Arrives
articles.description: Spot electricity prices in Japan surged on Monday to their highest level since August 2022 as gas demand is set to rise amid expectations of snowfall and colder weather in the coming days. Expected higher gas demand in the Chubu and Hokkaido regions, with gas now at its highest price in four years in both Asia and Europe, pushed Japan's nationwide day-ahead electricity price up by 6% on Monday compared to last week, per data from the Japan Electric Power Exchange cited by Bloomberg. The day-ahead spot power price in Japan on Monday soared to $0.24…

articles.title: America’s Biggest Oil Export Port Faces Thousands of Cyberattack Attempts
articles.description: The port that ships most of America's crude oil overseas is now fending off "hundreds or even thousands" of attempts to break into its systems every day, Port of Corpus Christi CEO Kent Britton told the Financial Times, as hackers step up a campaign against US ports and the cargo ships that call on them. The stakes at Corpus Christi are hard to overstate: about 60% of US crude exports, roughly 2.3 million barrels a day, flow out of the Texas port, Britton said in May. articles.title: Storms and Drones Disrupt Russia’s Oil Exports
articles.description: Russia’s oil exports from the Baltic Sea and the Black Sea have suffered loading delays and disruptions this month amid frequent storms and bad weather exacerbated by Ukrainian drone attacks and local alerts of attacks. At Russia’s key Baltic Sea ports, storms and bad weather have already caused delays in the loading of more than 10 oil tankers, traders and sources with knowledge of the schedules told Reuters on Monday. The storms are typical for this time of year, but this year Ukrainian attacks have also played a much larger role…

articles.title: What Is Trump Up To Bombing Iran’s Qeshm Island?
articles.description: The Republican Party’s loss of its majority in the Senate and the House of Representatives in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections has left President Donald Trump constrained in what he is able to achieve domestically. However, internationally, he is not so shackled. He needs no congressional approval to implement or increase economic tariffs. He holds on to the right to dictate the terms of U.S. alliances and treaties, including those related to the Russia-Ukraine War. Crucially as well, he retains the legal authority to escalate or de-escalate…

articles.title: Oil Slides Nearly 4% as Returning Supply Outweighs Gulf Attacks
articles.description: Crude prices deepened their slide on Monday even as Wall Street rallied on Nvidia's reinstatement of chief executive Jensen Huang, with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trading at its weakest level since late August. At 10:29 a.m. ET, WTI was down 3.5% at $80.50 per barrel, Brent was down 3.6% at 89.23 dollars, and U.S. natural gas futures had fallen 8.2% to 3.130 dollars per million British thermal units. Nvidia said it was reinstating Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board director, effective immediately, 11 days after he resigned.…

articles.description: Norway produced about 12.56 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day in October, up by about a fifth month-on-month and 5.6 percent year-on-year, according to preliminary official figures.

articles.title: Ukrainian Naval Drones Sink Russian Warship in Libya
articles.description: Ukrainian naval drones sank a Russian warship in the Libyan port of Benghazi, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, in Kyiv's first admitted strike on Libyan soil and the latest attack along the Mediterranean route that carries Russian oil to Asia. According to Zelenskiy, the seven drones sank the corvette Merkury, destroyed a Ka-27 helicopter along with it and hit the Russian dry cargo ship Angara, a vessel Moscow used to transport weapons. The strike followed a drone attack that set the Russian military-linked cargo ship Sparta II ablaze…

articles.description: US President Donald Trump may consider offering Ukraine security guarantees modeled on NATO's collective-defense commitments if he is convinced that the risk of another Russian invasion has been sufficiently reduced, special envoy Jared Kushner said. In a lengthy post on X on November 22, Kushner described Russia's reported willingness to discuss such guarantees as "a major step forward" and a potential indication that Moscow was serious about peace. articles.title: Brent Drops Below $90 as Wall Street Splits on 2027 Oil Outlook
articles.description: Brent crude will average $80 per barrel in 2027 as geopolitics and relatively low global inventories leave much of the world vulnerable to supply disruptions, Bank of America said in a new note. Brent fell 2.9% to 89.86 dollars by 9:02 a.m. ET on Monday, and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped 2.9% to 80.96 dollars. The bank kept its 2027 Brent forecast unchanged and projected the benchmark at $70 in 2028, with WTI at $74 and $66 over the same two years. BofA named geopolitics as the main force on prices and forecast global oil demand growth…

articles.title: South Korea Asks Qatar for Priority LNG Once Hormuz Reopens
articles.description: South Korea has asked Qatar to prioritize LNG supply to the Asian nation when traffic through the Strait of Hormuz normalizes, South Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said on Monday. Qatar, the world’s second-largest LNG exporter before the Iran war, has struggled to ship LNG carriers through the Strait of Hormuz, and gas flows have recovered only slightly, especially compared to the crude flows out of the Persian Gulf and the chokepoint. The Strait of Hormuz crisis hasn’t allowed many Qatari LNG cargoes to transit…
